Title: Dashboard SVGs declare role=img over 1,146 focusable descendants - an ARIA children-presentational conflict (found while adjudicating the 004/118-CRITIQUE A2 split) - 42 of the 43 `<svg role="img">` containers in the generated PROJECT_STATE.html hold interactive nodes, and 1,146 of the document's 1,150 `tabindex="0"` elements sit INSIDE a role=img subtree. ARIA specifies role=img as children-presentational, so that subtree is expected to be pruned from the accessibility tree - which means the per-node `<title>`s that A2 compliance was resting on may never reach a screen reader, and the interactive nodes may be unreachable. THIS IS THE CAUSE BOTH CRITIQUE DISAGREEMENTS WERE CIRCLING WITHOUT NAMING: 116-CRITIQUE (OPENCODE-GROK) PASSED A2 arguing the per-node titles cover it (they may be pruned); 004-CRITIQUE (OPENAI-SOL) FAILED A2 asking for container names (naming an image whose interactive children are pruned does not fix it); 118-CRITIQUE (OPENAI-SOL again) PASSED A2 on byte-identical evidence. The symptom they argued over was naming; the cause is the role. Fix: drop role=img from any SVG with focusable descendants, or replace it with role=group - the pattern the `.view` wrappers already use correctly (`role="group"` + aria-label); keep role=img only for genuinely non-interactive graphics, which then do each need their own accessible name. CAVEAT: AT implementations vary in how strictly they prune, so treat this as an authoring-conformance defect to correct rather than a proven end-user failure; confirm against a real screen reader if that is cheap. MECHANIZE (OI-9): ship a structural check on the EMITTED html - no element carrying role="img" may contain a focusable descendant, and any genuinely non-interactive role="img" must carry an accessible name. That check owns A2 and would have caught this without a critic. | WI-300 (f) OBLIGATION (2026-07-25 ruling): this row now CLOSES BY BINDING its anchor - land the fix, the test that owns the anchor, AND the child LLR+TC rows naming that test in Evidence, in the SAME commit. Title: A green suite silently hides 47 skipped tests when no POSIX shell is on PATH - make the environment gap ANNOUNCE itself (SN-008: a green never hides a skipped check). Measured 2026-07-26 on Windows: the same tree, the same commit, run twice. With `C:\Program Files\Git\bin` absent from PATH: 1540 passed, 54 skipped. With it present: 1587 passed, 7 skipped, zero failures - so 47 tests were not RUN and nothing said so above the -rs line nobody passes. The 47 are not marginal: 36 are `needs a POSIX shell and git on PATH` in test_pre_commit_hook.py, i.e. the tests guarding the COMMIT FLOOR itself, plus the dev-setup and agent-loop shell paths. Git for Windows ships sh.exe at Git\bin and Git\usr\bin but only puts Git\cmd on PATH, so this is the DEFAULT Windows developer state, not an exotic one - and the handoff's recorded '1579 passed, 7 skipped' vs a successor's '1540 passed, 54 skipped' is two sessions reporting incomparable greens without either noticing. Options, cheapest first: (a) a conftest session-header line stating N environment-gated skips and the one PATH entry that would close them; (b) the same, but FAIL the gate tier (check.py) when the count exceeds a declared floor, since a gate bar that skips its own floor tests is the dishonest-green case; (c) have dev-setup.sh --check report it. Prefer (a)+(b): announce always, gate at the gate. Do NOT auto-inject a PATH entry - silently repairing the environment hides the same fact one layer down.
Deliverable: DONE 2026-07-28. Option (a)+(b) as the row prefers, plus the single-source-of-truth move that makes the count honest. ONE declaration, conftest.ENV_GATES: each gate names its probe, what its absence COSTS, whether it is `required`, and a remedy computed for this machine - unreachable_posix_shell() finds an sh.exe that EXISTS but is off PATH and names the directory, so the message reads `put C:\Program Files\Git\bin on PATH` rather than an unactionable `no POSIX shell`. (a) ANNOUNCE: pytest_sessionstart prints the predicted banner on stderr before the first test (controller only, every run including -m smoke), and a new pytest_terminal_summary prints the MEASURED env-gated skip count after the last, with the explicit note that a pass total from this machine is not comparable with one from a fully-gated machine - the line whose absence let 1579/7 and 1540/54 be recorded as comparable greens. (b) GATE: test_prereq_toolchain.test_every_required_environment_gate_is_satisfied FAILS on any required gate; that module is SLOW-tiered, so the hard stop lands in the full suite - check.py's tests+coverage step and CI - while the commit bar stays passable on an unprovisioned box and keeps the banner. Same shape the interpreter floor already used, so no new tier and no new config surface. THE ENABLING CHANGE: the gate condition was four inline copies of shutil.which(sh) across test_pre_commit_hook (8 sites), test_onboard_devsetup (5), test_commit_msg_wi_trailer and test_pre_push_hook (module-level skipif) - the skips were real and the total was nobody's, which is exactly how 47 went uncounted. All now route through skip_without_env_gates / env_gate_skipif, which emit one shared reason string, and test_no_test_skips_on_a_hand_rolled_shell_probe scans tests/ to stop the copies growing back. NOT DONE, per the row: no PATH auto-injection - a harness that repairs its own environment hides the same fact one layer down. NOT COUNTED, deliberately: an os.name platform skip has no remedy, so counting it would make the number noise; test_count_ignores_an_unrelated_skip pins that. Title: A test run must not throttle the machine it runs on (owner-directed 2026-07-27: -so long as this computer and other personal computers are not throttled whenever this repo is running its tests-). Worker-count levers (ptc, setx PYTEST_XDIST_AUTO_NUM_WORKERS, the root conftest hook) cannot meet that: machine load is concurrent-runs x workers x child-processes, and they set the middle term only - a 12-worker run measured mean 59%/max 74% CPU with 42 python + 4 git processes live, because the slow tier is subprocess-per-test by design.
Deliverable: Root conftest.py gains pytest_configure -> a NAMED Windows job object with a HARD CPU rate cap (default 50%, PYTEST_CPU_CAP dials it, off/0/100 disables) plus a BelowNormal priority drop. The job bounds the whole tree (controller + every xdist worker + every subprocess they spawn) and, because it is NAMED, every pytest process joins the SAME job - so N concurrent runs and N train worktrees share ONE ceiling instead of multiplying it. Proven with a burner: 24 spinners = 100% CPU uncapped, 37.5% mean / 47% max under a 25% cap; probed live from an unrelated process mid-suite (ControlFlags=0x5, CpuRate=5000). Wall-clock cost negligible here (test_trace.py 20.4s capped vs 20.7s uncapped) because the suite is subprocess/IO-bound. CI opts out in test.yml + canary.yml (no desktop to protect, fewer cores, and a wall-clock smoke-budget job). POSIX degrades honestly to os.nice(5) - no cgroup-free hard cap exists there. Never fatal: any failure warns and the suite runs normally. Guards in tests/test_cpu_cap.py, all mutation-proven (flag 0x4->0x2 fails; not applying the cap fails; default 50->90 fails - that last one exposed a self-referential guard that had passed while the guarantee was withdrawn). TWO TRAPS PAID: HARD_CAP is 0x4 not 0x2 (0x2 is WEIGHT_BASED and rejects a rate), and QueryInformationJobObject(NULL) reports the IMMEDIATE job so it reads ControlFlags=0 inside an xdist worker's nested job - IsProcessInJob against the named handle is the correct instrument. || CORRECTED 2026-07-27 (WI-338 + 127-REVIEW-A BLOCKER 1). The 'every concurrent run joins the same named job and shares ONE ceiling / N runs total the cap' claim above is FALSE and was the headline of this WI. Windows permits assignment only into a job that is EMPTY or already in the process's own parent job chain, so a second run from a different process tree cannot join a job the first has populated: it falls back to a private job at the same percent and warns on stderr. Concurrent runs therefore MULTIPLY the cap - two can total ~100%. Measured directly: with a first tree holding the named job, two independent probes both reported PRIVATE while a CHILD of the first reported SHARED. Two further narrowings: an API failure leaves the run UNCAPPED, and POSIX's os.nice(5) is a priority bump, not a cap at all. What IS delivered - a tree-wide ceiling for ONE run, covering the xdist workers and the slow tier's per-test subprocesses - still answers the original problem that a worker count bounds workers and not processes, and the 50% default is unchanged. Now pinned by tests/test_cpu_cap.py::test_a_second_independent_run_gets_its_own_ceiling (first tree SHARED, child SHARED, independent second tree PRIVATE and warning), mutation-proven both ways; the pre-existing live-process test's OR over shared/private is kept but its comment no longer reads as 'asserts both' (MAJOR 2).

Title: Correct the FALSE CLAIMS 127-REVIEW-A refuted (BLOCKER 1 + BLOCKER 3). (1) The CPU cap's 'every concurrent run shares ONE ceiling' is asserted unconditionally in conftest.py's docstring, docs/status.md, docs/log.md, the archived WI-335 spec and the WI-335 Deliverable - but the code has THREE outcomes: compatible trees share the job, a FOREIGN process tree falls back to its own private 50% (so two runs can total ~100%), and an API failure runs uncapped; POSIX gets os.nice(5), which is not a cap at all. The reviewer's own run hit the fallback. Either implement a real machine-wide ceiling or narrow every assertion to what the code delivers. (2) WI-334's 'MOST of the blocks are the deliberate CLI preamble' is numerically false - reconstructed 34 CLI-preamble vs 50 other drifts - and 164 sanctions were signed on that premise, with the spec's own audit boxes left unchecked. Needs a truthful per-block classification, which WI-337 must land first (the counts are meaningless until the fingerprints are environment-independent).
Deliverable: DONE 2026-07-27. BOTH refuted claims corrected at every place they were signed. (1) THE CPU CAP. Measured rather than reasoned about: with a first process tree holding the named job, two independent probes both landed in a PRIVATE job while a CHILD of the first landed in the SHARED one. So Windows' rule (assignment is permitted only into a job that is EMPTY or already in the process's own parent job chain) means concurrent runs MULTIPLY the cap rather than total it - the parallel-train-worktree case the promise was written for is exactly the case it does not cover. What IS delivered is a TREE-WIDE ceiling for one run, which still answers the original problem (a worker count bounds workers, not the subprocess-per-test slow tier). Narrowed in conftest.py's docstring (now opening with an explicit what-this-does-and-does-not-guarantee block naming all four outcomes incl. the uncapped API-failure path and POSIX's os.nice(5) being a priority bump, not a cap), docs/status.md, docs/log.md's WI-335 entry, the archived WI-335 spec, and the WI-335 Deliverable. MAJOR 2 closed too: the live-process test's OR over shared/private is KEPT (it asserts the RATE, which is right) but its comment no longer claims to check both, and the guard that was missing now exists - test_a_second_independent_run_gets_its_own_ceiling asserts first-tree SHARED, child SHARED, second-independent-tree PRIVATE *and warning*, with the first assertion explicitly present so a fall-back-everywhere bug cannot satisfy the rest vacuously. Mutation-proven twice: forcing a private job reds the SHARED assertions, silencing the fallback warning reds only the warned=1 assertion. (2) THE CENSUS CLASSIFICATION, which WI-337 unblocked. All 208 blocks classified by READING them - the classifier refuses to finish while any block is UNCLASSIFIED, and it took four passes to get there. True distribution: cli 77 (37%), intra-module 64 (31%), spine-loader 21, markdown-table 11, declared-file 11, git-wrapper 9, wi-registry 5, module-path 4, okf-row 2, import-fallback 2, graph-walk 1, skills-materialize 1. So the CLI preamble IS the largest single class but is 37%, NOT 'MOST' - and nearly a THIRD of the census is not F5 duplication at all, it is intra-module debt WI-280 owns, which is the finding the original claim hid. The audit is recorded IN docs/dupes-allow, grouped, one section per class with its count and the reason the duplication is accepted, because that is where the next reader of a sanction looks; the header states plainly that --emit-census emits UNGROUPED lines so a future re-stamp must re-derive the grouping or say it didn't. || CORRECTED 2026-07-27 by 128-REVIEW-A, which refuted TWO of this row's claims. (a) BLOCKER 1: the CPU-cap correction above was ITSELF wrong, in the opposite direction. 'A second run from a different PROCESS TREE gets its own ceiling' is not the rule - AssignProcessToJobObject succeeds when the process is in NO job, or the target job is empty or in its own parent job chain - so an UNJOBBED second run joins the named job and really does share, while one that something has already jobbed cannot. The guard written for it was ambient-dependent: it passed here (every process is already jobbed) and FAILED on the reviewer's host, reporting SHARED. FIXED IN THIS BRANCH: the claim now states the condition in conftest.py/status.md/log/spec, and the test CONSTRUCTS the topology (a probe joins its own anonymous job first) so it asserts only what is universal - first tree SHARED, child SHARED, already-jobbed process PRIVATE with a warning AND a verified hard rate of 0x5/5000, which the previous guard never checked. (b) BLOCKER 2 is NOT fixed and is filed as WI-340: the 208-block audit reached 0 unclassified partly by bucketing all 64 same-file pairs as 'intra-module / WI-280 owns it', which is derivable from two path strings without reading the block and is the same reach-zero-by-broad-class failure this WI was correcting. The classification of the 67 CROSS-module blocks stands; the 64 intra-module ones are metadata, not a rationale.

Title: check_vendored.py hashes the CHECKOUT, not the content: it compares sha256 of the vendored file's RAW BYTES against the fetched upstream's, so a CRLF checkout of an LF-stored vendored doc reports false drift (every vendored file at once, since .gitattributes declares text eol=lf for them). Found 2026-07-27 auditing the other kit checkers for the same defect class as the duplicate-census fix that day (spec has the cross-reference); check_stubs, gen_arch_map and the ratchets were checked and are clean. Lower priority than WI-337 was: the step is not wired into docs/stack.ini here, is network-gated (it skips when upstream is unreachable) and WARNs unless --strict. Fix wants care that WI-337's did not: a vendored file may legitimately be binary, so normalize only what is declared text rather than stripping CR bytes blindly, and the guard must assert the SAME content hashes equal across line endings while genuinely different content still differs.
Deliverable: DONE 2026-07-28. content_digest(data) -> (digest, normalized) is what both sides of the comparison now go through: CRLF and lone CR collapse to LF for text, binary is hashed exactly as it is, and the WARN line NAMES which rule it applied - a comparison that silently changes its own basis is how the original defect stayed invisible. Both sides get the same treatment because the fetched remote may itself be served with either ending. THE CARE THE SPEC ASKED FOR, and the reason this is not WI-337 again: a vendored file may legitimately be BINARY, and stripping CR bytes from a PNG or an archive would corrupt the comparison - the opposite failure. looks_binary() sniffs a NUL byte (git's own heuristic) rather than trusting the extension, because an unknown extension must not silently opt a file OUT of the fix and a genuine binary must not be normalized into a false match. Empty content is text. Guards (6, tests/test_check_vendored.py) - one per Done-when clause: the same content matches across LF/CRLF/lone-CR; genuinely DIFFERENT content still differs, asserted twice (the spec's own words - both directions or it is half a guard, since a normalization that collapsed everything would pass the first test and be worthless); a binary file is sniffed, not normalized, and hashes byte-exact, with a PNG fixture that carries CRLF INSIDE its binary content on purpose; ordinary and EMPTY text take the normalizing path; and the mutation proof lives INSIDE the suite - it restates the pre-WI-339 raw-bytes predicate and asserts the defect reproduces before asserting the fix, so a successor can re-derive it rather than take a session's word for a hand-run mutation. Bar: smoke 509 passed; all 17 non-test G3 steps PASS.

Title: window_open() cannot see a single-phase repo's prior maturity, so a Draft there reads as ordinary early work (128-REVIEW-A MAJOR 3, residue). The G2/G3-floor fix closed the false POSITIVE (an early multi-phase repo). The false NEGATIVE remains and is structural: the discriminator reads only the CURRENT per-phase breakdown, and a Draft added to a previously-mature single-phase repo drops that phase to G0, erasing the very evidence the rule looks for - so no phase remains above `computed` and no advisory pass runs, which is the blind spot WI-336 exists to close. Any real fix needs PERSISTENT evidence rather than a snapshot: either derive_gate records a prior-maturity/high-water mark in the `# basis:` line, or a window becomes an explicit declared marker rather than something inferred from counts. Owner-shaped, because it changes what derive_gate publishes. Until then docs/status.md must keep stating the limit rather than implying the heuristic separates all cases.
Deliverable: DONE 2026-07-28 by MEASURING the counterfactual instead of inferring it, which turned an owner-shaped question into a mechanical one. The row offered two routes, both of which change what derive_gate publishes: a stored high-water mark, or an explicit window marker. Both were rejected - a high-water read from the artifact's own previous content makes a generated file depend on its own history and never falls back when a repo genuinely regresses; a declared marker re-introduces the hand-set gate the derived model exists to abolish. The evidence was already in the snapshot and nobody had asked for it: a Draft erases its PHASE's level, but it does not touch the sibling rows, which are still standing there. So derive_gate now publishes `ex-draft=` on the `# basis:` line - the SAME gate arithmetic run over the non-draft subset - and window_open reads it directly: a draft window needs ex-draft to clear G2 AND to sit above what the drafts produced. Pure function of the artifacts, no history, no self-reference, no owner decision required. The false negative is closed (mature single-phase repo + one Draft: computed=G0, per-phase=1=G0, ex-draft=G3 -> window) and the MAJOR-3 false positive stays closed at the source rather than by a floor heuristic (early multi-phase repo: removing the drafts recovers nothing, ex-draft=G1). Implemented by lifting the shared arithmetic into _raw_level(rows...) so compute() can ask it the counterfactual question - one function, called twice, rather than a second copy of the rules. The per-phase heuristic is KEPT as the fallback for a gate file written before the field existed, so an un-regenerated downstream repo keeps its old behaviour; regenerating docs/gate is the one migration step and `--check` reports it. Guards: three in test_derive_gate.py drive the real spine (a G3 single-phase repo reopened by a Draft, an early spine where ex-draft recovers nothing, and a clean repo where ex-draft == computed), five in test_advisory_during_window.py cover the consumer including both precedence directions with ex-draft and per-phase DISAGREEING, and one asserts the meta-repo's real docs/gate carries the field - without which every fixture assertion could pass while the producer published nothing. The mutation proof is in the suite: strip only `ex-draft=G3` from the winning fixture and the answer reverts to the documented defect. docs/status.md now states what the rule measures instead of describing a heuristic and its limit.

Title: Several signed measurements cannot be re-derived because their input state was transient (128-REVIEW-A MAJOR 4): the 28-LF/9-CRLF mixture behind '164 blocks on a mixed tree', the 67-file line-ending restoration and its byte-identity refusal check, the census classifier's 'four passes', and the 24.3s smoke wall-clock. Each was true when taken and none is reproducible from the repository, because the evidence lived in a working tree that the fix itself destroyed - which is precisely the shape of the false claims this branch has been correcting. The reviewer could corroborate the RESULTS (the committed 164-entry census; git proving no 67-file rewrite landed) but not the stated inputs or procedure. Decide the standing rule: either such observations are marked explicitly as historical and non-reproducible where they are signed, or a measurement that will be destroyed by its own fix must commit its evidence first (a filename manifest, the command, before/after hashes, raw timing output). Cheap and mechanical either way; the value is that it stops the next session inheriting a number it cannot check.
Deliverable: DONE 2026-07-28. Ruled: BOTH halves, in order, as one standing rule stated once in process-options.md "Signed measurements" (applies when a measured number is about to be written into a doc, log or registry row). (1) A measurement whose input its own fix will destroy must commit its evidence FIRST - the command, the manifest, before/after hashes, raw output - in the repo, not in a session transcript. (2) A number already taken on state that is gone is written as a historical, non-reproducible observation in the same sentence that states it. The reasoning worth keeping: such a number is not wrong, it is UNFALSIFIABLE, which to a reviewer is indistinguishable from one that was never true - that is how a false claim survives. Applied to all four sites 128-REVIEW-A named: the 28-LF/9-CRLF mixture (docs/dupes-allow) and the 67-file restoration (the archived WI-337 spec) are marked HISTORICAL with the independently checkable residue named beside them - the committed 164-entry census, and 128-REVIEW-A's own proof that no line-ending-only blob change landed; the classifier's "four passes" claim is gone, superseded by WI-340's re-triage which states its method rather than its effort; and the 24.3 s smoke figure now carries the command that re-derives it plus a fresh reading taken today (470 tests / 29.1 s), which is half (1) actually applied rather than described. Enforcement is honest: nothing can distinguish a live measurement from a recollection, so this is a Reviewer-tier rule and it is recorded as such in docs/enforcement-audit.md, with the evidence that the tier works - two adversarial reviews refuted or marked UNVERIFIABLE eight signed figures between them.

Title: Kit generators write GENERATED files with platform newlines, so a Windows run leaves an eol=lf artifact CRLF in the working tree. ALL 17 Path.write_text() call sites across project-trajectory/scripts pass no `newline` argument - counted by AST, not grep: 17 omit it and ZERO specify it, so on Windows every LF becomes CRLF on the way out. (The row first said '4 already do'; 129-REVIEW-A MAJOR 4 refuted that - the grep behind it had matched open(..., newline=) calls, which are a different API. Corrected here rather than restated.) Found 2026-07-28 on docs/gate, which .gitattributes declares eol=lf: `git ls-files --eol` reported `i/lf w/crlf` immediately after derive_gate.py regenerated it. Harmless for docs/gate specifically (git's clean filter normalizes the committed blob, and every reader strips), but this is the same defect CLASS as WI-337 - where a tool hashed the checkout's bytes and the resulting fingerprints were a property of the working tree, not the code - and WI-339 is a third instance in check_vendored.py. The general fix is a sweep: generated text is a repo artifact, so it should be written LF on every platform. Worth doing once, across all 17, with a guard that a freshly-generated artifact matches its committed blob byte for byte on both platforms.
Deliverable: DONE 2026-07-28. All 17 Path.write_text() call sites across the kit scripts converted to the open(..., newline=chr(92)+'n') form, plus THREE append sites the new guard found that the row had not counted - two of them appending to docs/log.md, so an integration on Windows was writing CRLF into it. Zero write_text sites remain and zero text-mode .open() lacks a newline policy, both verified by AST. THE IMPLEMENTATION CONSTRAINT, which is the whole reason this is not a one-liner: Path.write_text(newline=) is 3.13+ and the kit floor is 3.11, so the obvious fix is a TypeError on the oldest Python the kit claims. Found the hard way earlier the same day when a test caught the same slip in a fixture. The two-line open() form is inlined at each site rather than routed through a helper: the F5 independently-copyable rule means a helper would have to be copied into all eight scripts, and eight copies of a helper is a worse trade than sixteen extra lines with no new API. That decision is recorded in the census under lf-write-preamble (3 CROSS-SCRIPT blocks, triaged individually, not blanket-stamped). The SAME-FILE pair the change created - the two atomic-JSON writers in agent_dispatch - was EXTRACTED to _atomic_json instead, per WI-343 (F5 never covers a same-file copy), which also RETIRES the atomic-json census class and its distribution row. Guards (tests/test_generated_newlines.py, 5): two AST invariants - no write_text in a kit script, and every text-mode .open() declares newline= - plus a mutation proof that both predicates FIRE on the banned shapes and stay silent on the fixed form and on a BINARY write (a rule that banned open('wb') would be a different, wrong rule). The AST pair is what makes the fix stick, and it passes vacuously on a clean tree, which is exactly why the mutation proof is not optional. Then a behavioural guard runs REAL generators into a scratch tree and asserts no CR byte in what they wrote, scanning a directory or a file as appropriate - so the syntax rule is anchored to observed behaviour on whichever platform the suite runs. CORRECTION to the plan: gen_trajectory.py was NOT among the 17, so this change does NOT re-red perceptual-stale and no render critique is owed for it. `git ls-files --eol` shows no non-.ps1/.cmd/.bat file CRLF in the working tree. Title: Nothing enforces the one-physical-line rule that check_trajectory's staged-close scan DEPENDS on. check_trajectory.py:1478 documents the assumption in its own docstring - 'a WI row is one physical line (no embedded newlines)' - because it compares `git diff --cached --name-only` output and HEAD's registry text line-wise. No check asserts it. Demonstrated 2026-07-28: a WI row was written with a literal newline inside a quoted Title cell, the full trajectory validator reported CLEAN, and the only thing that surfaced it was git warning about mixed line endings in the working tree - i.e. luck. A row like that also renders as a broken cell in the dashboard's detail JSON and makes the row invisible to any line-based tool downstream. Fix: an integrity check in check_trajectory's validate() that fails on any cell containing CR or LF, with the WI id and column named, plus a test that writes such a row and asserts it is caught. Cheap, and it closes the gap between a documented assumption and an enforced one - the enforcement-audit question asked of a rule the code already relies on.
Deliverable: DONE 2026-07-28. check_trajectory.cell_integrity_errors(rows) reads the RAW registry cells before anything reasons about the graph they describe, and returns a hard error for any cell holding a CR or an LF, naming the WI id and the COLUMN - a bare 'row 47 is malformed' against a 352-row registry is not actionable, the cell is what the author has to find. Wired into main() beside load_wis's malformed/duplicate-id errors, which is the same class (a row the loader cannot be trusted to have read) rather than the warn-first coherence tier (a question about a row it read fine) - so it is an ERROR at every run, no --strict needed. Scoped deliberately to the WI registry: the line-wise HEAD comparison in staged_findings is what CREATES the requirement and it reads only this file; the spine registries are trace.py's. Kept OUT of load_wis so tests/test_wi_loader_sync.py's schedule-vs-check_trajectory drift lock is untouched. A broken id cell reports by ROW NUMBER, not a truncated id, because a truncated id is worse than none - it looks real and matches nothing. Guards (tests/test_trajectory.py, 5 tests): the offending registry is written through csv.writer rather than by hand-embedding a newline, so it exercises the real quoting path that made the defect invisible, and the test asserts the premise first (one CSV row really does span two physical lines). LF caught, CR caught, broken id cell reported positionally, a mutation twin with the newline removed asserted CLEAN, and - the finding itself pinned - a test that load_wis, validate and ssot_findings ALL pass on that row, so the guard cannot start silently riding on some unrelated rule. Four mutants (check unwired, CR dropped from the detected set, column name dropped from the message, row-number fallback reverted to the truncated id) each fail the suite. Found while writing the guard: Path.read_text(newline=) is 3.13+, so a 3.11-floor kit must use open() - the test caught it. Module-size ratchet re-stamped 2063 -> 2135, reviewed bump with the reason in the log; check_trajectory.py has now taken FOUR upward bumps with no decomposition between them, which is a cost the WI-280 deferral is accruing. Bar: smoke 490 passed / 27.9 s; the 16 non-test G3 steps PASS.

Title: The census-audit guard still admits a catch-all under two labels instead of one (129-REVIEW-A BLOCKER 1). WI-340's anti-catch-all rule - a class charged to a WI must name a WI that exists, is open, and whose row names every module in the class - was DRIVEN and bypassed by the reviewer: all 64 same-file blocks were rebuilt into two arbitrary 32-entry classes `misc-a`/`misc-b` plus one synthetic open WI whose Title merely LISTED the module basenames, and every one of the six checks returned clean. Two rules are too weak. tests/test_dupes_census_audit.py:314-329 bans only a single MAJORITY class, so an even split evades it; and :220-246 accepts ownership on a substring match, so a keyword-stuffed row satisfies it without the WI having any relationship to the code. The property actually wanted is that a class states a rationale a reader can CHECK against the block - which is not the same as any predicate over path strings and WI text, and may not be fully mechanizable; if it is not, say so and move the residue to the enforcement audit as a Reviewer-tier rule rather than leaving a guard that advertises a property it does not hold. Whatever replaces it must be tested against the reviewer's exact bypass (an even split plus a cosmetic WI row), not only against a renamed single bucket.

`ex-draft` misses a mature spine reopened by flipping an EXISTING child to Draft, and the obvious fix creates the mirror false positive (129-REVIEW-A MAJOR 2, plus a counter-measurement taken while triaging it). The reviewer drove a real spine - Verified SR, one TC, its SOLE LLR changed to Draft - and got `computed=G0 ex-draft=G1 window=False`: excluding the Draft LLR also removes the structural evidence that the SR is decomposed, so the counterfactual calls a mature G3 chain undecomposed. Confirmed here on the shipped code. BUT the correction the review proposes - keep the Draft child's structural role while dropping its maturity contribution - was measured too, on the same shipped functions, and it fires on an EARLY project: a ratified-but-unverified SR (Planned) with a drafted LLR and a TC reads ALT `ex-draft=G2` against `computed=G0`, i.e. window=True, which is exactly the nag that 127-REVIEW-A MAJOR 5 ruled out. So this is NOT a one-line fix and must not be treated as one; this branch has already shipped two corrections that were wrong in the opposite direction. A lead worth testing: in the mature case the SR is `Verified` and in the early case it is `Planned`, so the two are separable by SR maturity rather than by structure - but check what that does to the multi-phase G2 cases before adopting it. Whatever lands must pin BOTH spines above as producer and consumer tests, each mutation-proven.

A WI's `Status` is the one ATTESTATION in this repo with no reconciler, so it can disagree with the evidence indefinitely and nothing says so. Widened 2026-07-28 from the single symptom that exposed it (WI-328 sat `queued` for a day with all six Done-when boxes ticked, the LLR Rationale column and the IF v2 bumps shipped, and SafetyClass=spine serializing the whole project behind finished work) to the general rule the symptom is an instance of. THE DESIGN QUESTION, ASKED AND ANSWERED (owner, 2026-07-28): should completion be DERIVED instead, like the gate? No - and the reason is already in this registry. The evidence a deriver would read is the `WI:` commit trailer, which agent_common.latest_trailer_evidence ALREADY folds into built/blocked sets for the dispatcher; but a trailer means 'a commit CLAIMS this WI', not 'the work is right'. WI-336 is the counterexample: its code landed while its row stayed `queued`, and that was CORRECT, because a review had refuted three of its claims - a deriver would have flipped it to done and been wrong. `deferred`/`blocked`/`retired` are not derivable at all, being decisions not outcomes. Completion is an attestation, and attestation is where the derivation chain bottoms out: derive_gate computes the gate FROM declared Status cells, so deriving those in turn just moves the turtle. WHAT IS MISSING is not derivation but RECONCILIATION - the same shape every other declared-vs-computed pair here already has (derive_gate --check recomputes and fails on drift; every generator carries --check). Build one reconciler in check_trajectory that compares the declared cell against every completion signal available and reports DISAGREEMENT, never auto-flipping: (a) an OPEN row whose SpecRef resolves to a spec with >=1 `- [x]` and zero `- [ ]` left; (b) the mirror - a `done` row whose spec still has unticked boxes (40c92f6 exists because S5 was ticked before it was true); (c) an OPEN row named by a `WI:` trailer on an integrated commit; (d) a `done` row with an empty Deliverable (currently zero, so it ships as a zero-to-zero guard). WARN plain, ERROR under --strict, matching R-E/R-F, and vacuous-until-armed on a repo with no specs or trailers. Fail LOUDLY and let a human resolve - an auto-flip would re-create exactly the false completion WI-336 and 40c92f6 were both corrections of.
Deliverable: DONE 2026-07-28. completion_reconciliation_findings(root, wis) compares the declared Status cell against the completion evidence and returns (kind, message) pairs so the caller tiers them without pattern-matching prose. Three signals: spec-says-finished (an OPEN row whose own spec has >=1 ticked Done-when box and none left - the WI-328 shape), spec-says-unfinished (a done row whose own LIVE spec still has unticked boxes and which no open WI cites - 40c92f6's shape), and trailer-claims-it (an OPEN row named by a WI: trailer reachable from HEAD). Never auto-flips: an auto-flip would re-create exactly the false completion WI-336 and 40c92f6 were both corrections of. THREE SCOPING DECISIONS, EACH MEASURED RATHER THAN ASSUMED. (1) The done side reads LIVE specs only. Run over the archive it produced 38 findings and neither class was actionable - some are a self-referential terminal box (`Commit bar green; row done, spec archived`, untickable at the moment you would tick it), the rest are closes that never ticked; for a WI closed weeks ago whose Deliverable and log entry carry the record the only available action is cosmetic, and a check whose recommended action is nothing is the wall of warns WI-308 recorded as how a check earns its own ignore. The moment that IS actionable gets its own check: staged_completion_findings warns at the closing commit, where the spec is still live and both homes can be made to agree in one change. (2) A WI's spec is NAME-IDENTIFIED (docs/specs/WI-###.md, then the archived form), never whatever SpecRef points at - measured before this rule existed, following SpecRef reported WI-324's work FINISHED out of ticks WI-321 had made, because WI-324 cites the shared WI-321 effort doc. (3) The Done-when tally is a SECTION, bounded by heading LEVEL: a subdivided Done-when keeps its boxes, a sibling heading ends it - WI-321.md carries WI-324's remaining boxes under a sibling `## Split off, deliberately`, and folding those in attributes one WI's unfinished work to another. Migration checklists are steps, not evidence, and do not count. DEVIATION FROM THE ROW, taken on the row's own argument and pinned by a test: the trailer signal WARNS and never joins the exit code, not even under --strict. The row rules that Status stays an attestation precisely because a trailer CLAIMS a WI rather than attesting it, and cites WI-336 - code landed, row correctly left queued, a review having refuted three of its claims. Erroring there blocks the G3 gate for the length of that rework with no honest way out but a false close. Spec evidence is different in kind: a ticked box IS an attestation, so its disagreement with the row is a contradiction between two homes for one fact and gates. The fourth signal the row asked for - a done row with an empty Deliverable - is deliberately NOT reimplemented: R-A already makes it a hard ERROR at every run, strictly stronger than this tier, and a second weaker copy of a live rule is the duplication the working agreement forbids. Pinned by a test so the omission reads as a decision, not a gap. Guards: 18 tests, every signal driven against a constructed spec and every one paired with the twin that must stay silent. Six mutants (no-ticked-box reads as done, standing check reads the archive, any heading ends Done-when, open-citer suppression removed, trailer joins the exit code, migration checklists count) each fail the suite. Complexity: main() 21 -> 22, a reviewed +1, with the tier DECISION extracted to tier_completion_findings rather than written as two more branches. Module size 2135 -> 2495, reviewed bump - and the fifth consecutive one on this module, so check_trajectory.py is named as WI-280's concrete next slice with its measured number. Bar: smoke 490 passed / 24.8 s; all 17 non-test G3 steps PASS.

Title: Spec archival relinks INBOUND links but not the moved spec's OWN outbound ones, so archiving a link-rich spec strands it. WI-288 made _archive_closed_specs link-aware in one direction: _relink_archived_specs (agent_dispatch.py) redirects links that POINT AT a spec it just moved. The mirror half is missing - the spec moves from docs/specs/ to docs/archive/specs/, one level deeper, so every relative link INSIDE it (`](../log.md)`, `](../requirements/work-items.csv)`, `](../../project-trajectory/PROCESS.md)`) now resolves one directory short. The loop cannot catch these: it only rewrites a link whose target resolves to a MOVED SOURCE, and these targets did not move - the file did. Demonstrated 2026-07-28 archiving WI-328's spec BY HAND: six broken links, check_docs went from OK to FAIL immediately. Latent rather than never-hit, which is why WI-288 did not find it - most specs carry few relative links, so it only bites on a link-rich one, and then it reddens the composed tree at INTEGRATION, exactly the late-surfacing failure WI-288 existed to stop. Fix: at archival, re-relativise the moved file's own relative link targets by resolving each against the OLD directory and re-computing it against the NEW one (leave scheme/anchor/absolute targets alone, preserve any #fragment and the link TEXT, keep the newline discipline). Same indivisible-ritual rule as WI-288: move, relink-inbound and relink-outbound are one operation no caller can do two thirds of. Guard with a spec fixture that carries one link at each depth (`./`, `../`, `../../`) plus an anchor and an http URL, archived through the REAL function, then check_docs run over the result.
Deliverable: DONE 2026-07-28. _rebase_moved_spec_links(wt, moves) is the mirror WI-288 left unbuilt: at archival each moved spec's OWN relative link targets are resolved against the OLD directory and re-relativised against the NEW one. The inbound loop structurally cannot reach these - it rewrites a link whose TARGET resolves to a moved source, and here the targets did not move, the document did - which is why the two are separate functions rather than one. Left alone, for the same reason in each case: a bare #fragment, a scheme-ish or protocol-relative URL, and a root-relative /path all resolve independently of the holding directory, so moving the file cannot break them. The #fragment and the link TEXT survive; line endings are preserved. Wired INSIDE _archive_closed_specs beside the inbound half, so the ritual stays indivisible - its docstring now says a caller cannot do two thirds of it, and a test pins that the inbound redirect was not lost while adding the outbound rebase. The new half created a same-file duplication and check_dupes went RED, which is the F5 rule working (it buys cross-SCRIPT copy-ability, never a same-file copy), so TWO primitives were extracted rather than sanctioned: _rewrite_md_links (the traversal, the leave-it-alone None contract, and the newline="" I/O discipline, shared by both rewriters, since only the per-link DECISION differs between them) and _resolvable_link (the is-this-a-repo-relative-path test, with skip_absolute for the one asymmetry - a /path cannot be broken by moving the HOLDER but can be by moving the TARGET, so only the rebase half excuses it). Guards (6, tests/test_agent_dispatch_decisions.py): a fixture carrying a link at each depth (same dir, ./, ../, ../../, sideways) plus an anchor, an absolute path and an http URL, archived through the REAL _archive_closed_specs and then checked with the REAL check_docs - and the MUTATION TWIN moves the same fixture without the rebase and asserts check_docs FAILS, so the guard demonstrably reproduces the defect it fixes. Plus: the #fragment survives, the link text is untouched, a same-directory move is a no-op, CRLF is preserved with no lone LF introduced, and both halves of the ritual still run. Found while writing them: check_docs does not resolve root-relative links at all, so that shape is asserted on the decision function instead of end-to-end. Module size 3923 -> 4028, reviewed bump. Bar: smoke 497 passed; all 17 non-test G3 steps PASS.

Title: A WI's SpecRef anchor is never validated, so a row can cite a heading that does not exist. check_trajectory's R-E resolves a SpecRef by splitting on '#' and testing only that the PATH exists (check_trajectory.py:1113-1130); the fragment is discarded unread. Found 2026-07-28 closing WI-326, whose row had cited 'docs/log.md#2026-07-26--wi-326-a-green-that-hid-47-tests' since it was filed - a truncated slug matching no heading in that file. Nothing surfaced it for two days; it surfaced only because the close wrote the same anchor into a markdown LINK, where check_docs rejected it immediately. So the identical reference is enforced in one home and unchecked in the other, which is the WI-308 doc-refs class one registry over: a citation whose target moved or was never there reads as traceable and is not. Fix: have R-E resolve the fragment too when the path is a markdown file - slugify the file's ATX headings the same way check_docs already does and reuse that, do not write a second slugifier - and report the WI id, the ref, and the nearest matching heading, because a wrong anchor is nearly always a stale or truncated one rather than an invented one. Guard with a row citing a real file and a bogus anchor, asserting it is caught, plus its twin citing a real anchor asserting it is not; run the new check over the live registry before landing, since more rows than WI-326 may be wrong.
Deliverable: R-E now resolves the ANCHOR half of a doc#anchor SpecRef, not just the path: specref_findings() reuses check_docs.parse_doc for the anchor set (one slugifier, so a reference cannot pass as a SpecRef and fail as a link) and reports the nearest heading, prefix-first so a TRUNCATED slug names its full form. Lazy sibling import degrades to path-only rather than breaking the shipped hook. Extracted from ssot_findings to stay under the C901 limit. Live registry measured clean (6 anchored rows, re-derived at close); the test that pinned "anchor ignored by R-E" became the positive case.

Title: `--gate` is silently ignored by `--run-step`/`--run-steps`, so the documented per-WI bar is weaker than it reads and `--list` advertises a command that is not the one run. check.py resolves the plan at gate "all" for both flags (check.py:1274 and :1293) no matter what --gate says. Measured 2026-07-28: `check.py --gate G3 --list` prints `check_trajectory.py --strict` while `check.py --gate G3 --run-steps trajectory` executes `check_trajectory.py` with no --strict. `trajectory` is the ONLY step that differs, because it alone keys on `gate in ("G2","G3")` (check.py:469) while every other gate-conditional step includes "all" - but it is the step carrying the R-A..R-E, status.md forward-only and perceptual-stale promotions, so the whole coherence tier silently degrades to warn. This BIT the WI-354 session: the handoff's 18-step block reported 18/18 PASS while two real G3 errors were live (a done WI id in status.md, and the new CMP-001->CMP-003 import with no declared IF seam); both surfaced only on a direct --strict run. NOT a one-line fix: resolving at "all" is DELIBERATE for the shipped pre-commit hook (check.py:461-467), and the hook passes no --gate - but --gate DEFAULTS to the repo's active gate, so naively honouring `gate` would arm --strict in the commit floor, which that comment forbids. The fix needs an explicit-vs-default sentinel (argparse default=None) so an explicitly passed --gate is honoured while the hook's defaulted call stays warn-first, and must pin BOTH halves as tests: the hook's floor stays warn-first, and `--gate G3 --run-steps trajectory` really does gate. Also decide what `--list` should print, since today it renders a plan --run-steps will not execute.

The census audit guard checks every distribution ROW against its section but never the declared TOTAL, so docs/dupes-allow's header can drift silently. Measured 2026-07-28 during WI-347: the header read 'The distribution (207 blocks)' while the sections held 201 fingerprint lines, and all 13 audit tests passed - because the guard compares each row's count to its own section header, every header did match its own lines, and nothing compares the sum to reality. The 'By disposition' summary line was stale the same way, reading 'extract 35' while the rows summed to 29. One block of the 6-block gap is explained (WI-341 merged two adjacent spine-loader runs); the rest was never tracked down, which is exactly the cost of an unchecked aggregate. Fix: assert the declared total equals the summed section counts AND the emitted census size, and assert the by-disposition line against the sections - or generate the whole header block from the sections, which is the rule this repo already applies to derived numbers. Guard it by mutating the header total and confirming red; a guard that cannot fail is the defect being fixed here.
